title: Compact workspace chips + contextual micro-rail: progressive IA and routing prototype for Console
creator: Lena Hartmann
description: Design a compact, high-density workspace switcher and a contextual micro-rail to surface route-level controls (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) without overwhelming the left rail. Prototype interaction patterns for keyboard-first flows, progressive disclosure, and clear routing semantics for deep links and shared links.
background: Current Console left rail is large and uses full workspace tiles which causes vertical churn for teams with many workspaces. Teams frequently need to pivot between dashboards, rollout controls, and per-model cost views; those pivots are buried in nested nav or require a separate search flow. Previous sidebar explorations favored a full-width reframe; this ticket explores a compact chip-based switcher paired with a lightweight contextual rail (micro-rail) that appears inline when a route has tool-level controls.
goals: Reduce vertical space used by workspace switcher by at least 40% on typical 1080p screens
Provide single-click access to route-level tooling: dashboards, rollouts, cost breakdowns
Preserve deep-link stability: shareable URLs must open to the same route and micro-rail state where applicable
Support keyboard navigation and screen-reader semantics for accessibility
Surface quick cost pivots (last-24h / last-30d) without leaving current route
constraints: Must use existing left-rail width constraints for 3 responsive breakpoints
Micro-rail must not require a full page reload; should be client-side rendered and route-aware
No changes to existing backend routing schema — only client-side routing and query params allowed
Design must account for both hosted and dedicated tenants where workspace names can be long
decisions: Adopt a compact workspace chip (avatar + truncated name + chevron) with overflow menu for full list
Introduce contextual micro-rail: a second-level horizontal rail that slides out from under the primary nav when route metadata indicates available tooling
Encode micro-rail state in URL query param `?micro=tool:rollout` to maintain shareability
Keyboard nav: Tab focuses chips, Enter opens chip; pressing 'M' toggles micro-rail for focused route
Progressive disclosure: show only the most-used route tools by default, with a 'More' menu exposing full toolset
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates workspace chip layout and overflow behavior (desktop + tablet)
Micro-rail opens and closes without full route reload; query param persists across refresh
Accessibility: micro-rail items have ARIA roles and keyboard focus order validated in prototype
Usability test (5 participants) shows <10s median time to switch workspace + open rollout control
Design handed off to ENG with component spec and responsive tokens, plus example GH ticket for implementation
stakeholder_feedback: PM (Diego Morales): prefers query-param approach to preserve GA tracking for rollouts
Eng lead (Maya Sullivan): requests micro-rail initial render to be lazy-loaded to avoid bundle bloat
Security (Jon Park): flagged that micro-rail must not expose controls if the user lacks permission; needs server-side guard
Product Ops (Ravi Patel): likes the cost quick-pivots but asked for a lightweight sparkline in the chip hover state
engineering_deps: ENG-15812: client-side routing utility to parse and hydrate micro-rail state
ENG-16245: RBAC checks for route-level controls (backend)
next_steps: Run 5 moderated usability tests with platform engineers and PMs (scheduled week of 2026-03-15)
Incorporate feedback and produce Handoff package (components, tokens, interaction spec)
Draft GH implementation epic and break into engineering tickets: responsive, routing, RBAC
Schedule a design review with Security and Accessibility to finalize ARIA patterns
